# Independent audit of the diagonal-envelope double-knot reduction

**PASS.** Audited
`candidate a38c69b78fd106d1` independently.
This audits its compact-domain reduction only, not the missing sharp
global envelope bound.

At every positive radius, beta<=at gives q_h>=t r_h>0. At radius-zero
transitions an active envelope is O(r_h^d), so the stated zero extension
is continuous. On a>=epsilon only finitely many h occur. At fixed beta,
active envelopes are affine in a while positive-part mass powers are
convex; mass-zero knots require no additional exceptional maxima.

On a left knot a=d beta+t/H, its admissible hard-tilt condition is exactly
beta<=t/H. The left slack is t(1−j/H), giving the asserted active indices,
and slack/q<=1. Direct differentiation gives expression (6). Its ratio
test has logarithmic-derivative numerator (d−3)x−d<0 on [0,1]. At x=1
the exact remaining numerator is 3d+2 over (d+1)^2. The right-envelope
Hessian is exactly (7); slack_R<=p follows from p>=t r and makes its
bracket negative, including j=0.

On a right knot a=t/H−d beta(1+1/H), its right slack is more explicitly

    (1−j/H)(t−d beta).

Positivity of a forces beta<t/[d(H+1)], so the right-active indices are
indeed j<H. The derivative ratio eta=dj(1+1/H)/(j+1) lies in [0,d].
Direct differentiation of d^d[p^(d−1)r−d p^d] gives exactly (8).
The bound A*d<=d^2/(d+1)^2<1 makes that quadratic decreasing on the
whole required eta interval; its value at d is (6). The left-envelope
second derivative is precisely (9). The hard-tilt threshold q>=t r
gives slack_L<=q, and its bracket is strictly negative for j>0.
The j=0 left envelope is constant. Thus the two knotwise convexity
arguments retain the correct comparison directions and no curvature
term is lost or counted twice.

Solving the two knot equations gives the displayed beta and a exactly.
Their hard-tilt condition simplifies to H<=(2d+1)J+d, while beta>=0
gives J<=H. J=0 is exactly the own-right activation beta=t/d. Relevant
H and J are finite on a>=epsilon: at a left knot r_H=dq_H>=0, hence
H<=1/a; at a right knot r_H=dp_H>0, hence H<1/a. The beta=0 and
hard-tilt endpoints, including zero-radius coincidences, are retained.

On beta=at the left envelope equals Gamma r_h^d termwise. On a=1 its
central left envelope is Gamma. On beta=0 the envelope sum is exactly
2Gamma S_1((d+1)a). The decreasing left-sum bound for S_d and the convex
trapezoid bound for S_1 have the stated directions and constants. These
three outer edges therefore have nonpositive deficit.

The small-slope edge a=epsilon remains explicitly in the theorem. Nothing
in the audit converts this compact-domain statement into an unrestricted
maximum, removes that edge, or compares every double knot to H=1,J=0.
The d=2 appearances of negative powers occur only at positive active
thresholds and do not invalidate the algebra or continuity argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
